extracted.intended_audience: DeKalb County School System administrators, Department of Personnel, school principals, and affected contractual and auxiliary employees
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative policy and detailed procedures for conducting reductions in force (RIF) in the DeKalb County School System, specifying causes for RIF, prioritization rules, displacement/termination phases, notification, recall, certification and appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to avoid reduction in force
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the DeKalb County Board of Education to avoid exercising reduction in force procedures through planned management techniques including comprehensive budgeting, maintaining adequate financial reserves, projecting student enrollments, projecting staffing needs, absorbing vacancies arising from attrition, contracting teachers employed midyear for the balance of the year only with no commitments for further employment, and when necessary nonrenewing contracts for teachers having less than three complete academic years of service in the DeKalb County School System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes proactive management actions to prevent RIF before resorting to personnel reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible causes/conditions triggering RIF
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction in force actions may be necessary when overstaffing occurs due to: inadequate funds; insufficient student enrollment to merit continuation of a program; decline in average daily attendance (ADA); shift in selection of courses by students; decline in need for services rendered by a position classification; return of contractual personnel from sabbatical leaves of absence; discontinuation of a program by action of the Board; budget reduction by action of the Board; introduction of the four quarter school year; change in pupil-teacher ratios; closure or change in purpose of one or more schools or educational centers; reorganization; legal mandates; judicial decrees; or other exigencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed conditions constitute legitimate bases for declaring surplus personnel and initiating RIF procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles governing RIF implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction in force must be accomplished by using fair, efficient, and consistent procedures while constantly providing for the optimal welfare of the students of the DeKalb County School System. Reduction in force actions shall be based on position classifications, EEOC classifications, lengths of continuous service, and certification if applicable. Reduction in force actions must not adversely affect judicial decrees. First consideration is to cause minimal disruption in the academic program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the evaluative axes and higher-order priorities (student welfare, minimal disruption, compliance with court orders) that must guide all RIF decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superintendent staffing assessment factors and protected positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on student enrollment, funding sources, legal mandates, priorities, State standards for public schools, accreditation standards, and other related factors, the Superintendent of Schools will assess staffing needs and determine surplus personnel by position classifications as well as the date such reductions are needed. The Superintendent may designate selected position classifications as having protected positions within those classifications to maintain vital programs, functions, and/or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Superintendent has authority to evaluate multiple contextual factors and to create protected positions to preserve essential programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment of positions authority and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Superintendent shall have the authority to approve allotment formulas for staffing schools. Allotted positions will be determined by each position classification in each school using approved allotment formulas. Approved positions for systemwide departments will be designated by the Superintendent and will be funded through an annual budget or amended budget. Additional approved positions may be designated for compensatory education, special education, vocational education, grant positions, and emergency conditions requiring temporary additional staffing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who sets staffing formulas and which positions may be exceptions (grants, emergencies, categorical programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service lists maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Personnel shall maintain length of service lists of personnel by position classifications, EEOC classifications, continuous service dates, and certification if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lists are the operative records used to determine ordering in RIF and displacement; accuracy is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification definitions and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification relates to Georgia teaching certificates issued by the Georgia Department of Education. Dual/multiple certification implies holding endorsements in two or more fields or multiple certificate types; dual/multiple certification will qualify an employee for the benefit of two or more reduction in force options in the displacement process. A teacher will be considered for RIF in each field in which certified and will be placed on the service list that offers the greatest protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding multiple certifications increases displacement/placement options and protection from RIF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position classification and active assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each employment position classification has a position name and numeric code; each employee is classified under a single position classification based on active assignment or last active assignment if on leave. For contractual personnel, the active assignment is the certification endorsement area in which the teacher is actively teaching (or previously taught if on leave) for 51% of the duty assignment at the time RIF is declared; those not spending 51% on one duty assignment are categorized by the assignment covering the greatest portion of the day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the single classification under which an employee is considered for RIF and displacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEOC classification use
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifications established by EEOC (Alaskan Native, American Indian, Asian, Black (not of Hispanic origin), Hispanic, Pacific Islander, White (not of Hispanic origin)) will be used for RIF actions except that Hispanic and White will be considered as a single class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEOC grouping is an explicit axis for service lists and RIF calculations; note the special treatment combining Hispanic and White.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous service date and length of service definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'continuous service date' is the date an employee reports for duty in a full-time position which marks the beginning of a continuous employment period with no interruptions other than approved leaves and no changes to part-time or substitute status. 'Length of service' is the time employed continuously with the same restrictions. Resignation and subsequent reemployment resets continuous service date; resignation, discharge, termination, or nonrenewal cancel all length of service rights under the RIF procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes precise rules for accrual and loss of RIF seniority rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking in length of service
rubrics_metrics.description: If continuous service dates are the same, ties are broken by: (1) date 'Statement of Acceptance' was signed for the most recent period; (2) if same, date of receipt of earliest 'Application for Employment'; (3) if same, earliest date of receipt of the first written communication regarding employment; (4) if still tied, by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an ordered set of deterministic tiebreakers before resorting to random lot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial determination of general surplus personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Superintendent assesses by position classifications the staff necessary for efficient operation; personnel employed in excess of necessary staff as determined by the Superintendent will be declared surplus personnel subject to RIF. Superintendent may designate protected positions within classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaring surplus is an administrative determination by the Superintendent using the previously listed assessment factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of tentative surplus personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Personnel will calculate the quantity of surplus personnel by position classifications, EEOC classifications, and fields of certification if applicable, and then identify tentative surplus personnel by position classifications, EEOC classifications, lengths of continuous service, and certification; consideration will also be directed to court decrees and protected positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational step that translates position-level surplus counts into specific employees identified as tentatively surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary termination for performance/other non-RIF causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment may be terminated or suspended for reasons relating to quality of performance: incompetency, insubordination, willful neglect of duties, immorality, inciting students to violate law/ordinance/policy/rules, or any other good and sufficient cause. Also for failure to secure/maintain necessary training or valid certification. Such terminations processed per Georgia Codes and not as RIF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates performance-based dismissals from RIF procedures; employees dismissed for these reasons are not covered by RIF protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I: Termination without displacement categories and order
rubrics_metrics.description: When RIF necessary, position classifications with surplus personnel will be subject to termination without displacement in the following order: (a) contractual personnel (excluding protected) unable to obtain valid infield Georgia teaching certificates; (b) contractual personnel (excluding protected) able to obtain only provisional certification at the B-4 level; (c) contractual personnel (excluding protected) able to obtain only out-of-field certification and/or probationary PA series and who have less than three complete academic years of service in the system; (d) auxiliary personnel (excluding protected) in surplus classifications who have less than six months service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies priority categories for immediate termination (no displacement) based on certification status and length of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of personnel on leaves (Phase I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees on leaves of absence at the time of RIF will remain on leaves in accordance with original leave agreements; at conclusion of leave, separations become final with cancellation of benefits for those in Phase I. Employees subject to RIF on leave may apply for employment along with other qualified applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that being on leave does not shield Phase I categories from eventual separation and termination of benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination by length of service (Phase I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel tentatively selected for termination will be terminated in the order of shortest lengths of service within the respective length of service lists of the designated position classifications. Termination results in loss of all employment benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within each Phase I category, shortest service employees are terminated first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II: Displacement procedures for personnel with <3 complete academic years
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel with less than three complete academic years in surplus positions will have a choice of: (1) resignation, (2) leave of absence, (3) reassignment to a position having equivalent salary/prestige/responsibility if available, or (4) reassignment to a position having less salary/prestige/responsibility if available. In each displacement, the reassigned employee must be qualified and certified if infield certification is necessary; an employee cannot displace someone with greater length of continuous service. Notices must be delivered by designee or registered mail; failure to select an alternative by the deadline results in termination and loss of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines displacement options, qualification/certification requirements, seniority protection, and notice/response mechanics for <3-year employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction in force levels (hierarchy for displacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Displacement decisions start with highest level positions in the following order: (1) Associate Superintendents; (2) Assistant Superintendents and others on Salary Schedule Y; (3) Directors on Schedule X; (4) Assistant Directors on Schedule W; (5) High School Principals and Schedule S; (6) Elementary Principals and Schedule R; (7) Assistant Principals Schedule P; (8) Counselors Schedule N; (9) Social Workers Schedule M; (10) Teachers Schedule L; (11) Administrative Assistants Schedule K; (12) Administrative Assistants Schedule J; (13) Counselors Schedule G; (14) Audiologists Schedule F; (15) Teachers, Librarians, others on Schedule A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies ordered levels used to conduct displacement across the system; Level #15 is final reassignment level for contractual personnel (with auxiliary exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of surplus contractual personnel after displacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers and certificated personnel on level #15 after all displacements are subject to termination and have choice of (1) resignation or (2) leave of absence not to exceed one year. Employees selected for displacement at higher levels who lack appropriate certification for reassignment are also subject to termination with same choices. Contractual employees who previously served in auxiliary positions (>6 months during continuous employment) may displace personnel in previous auxiliary classification and lower auxiliary levels for which qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives choices available to displaced contractual personnel and special auxiliary-recall displacement rights for prior auxiliary service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of surplus auxiliary personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary personnel with more than six months' service will be subject to displacing other auxiliary personnel in descending order of each position's maximum progression step (starting Step 63 down to Step 1). After displacements, surplus auxiliary personnel are subject to termination and have choice of (1) resignation or (2) leave of absence not to exceed one year. Notices must be delivered by designee or registered mail; responses must be in person or registered mail; failure to select alternative by deadline results in termination and loss of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary displacement prioritizes pay-step seniority within auxiliary classifications and provides the same notice/response rules as for contractual employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of personnel on leaves during displacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees on leaves at the time of RIF will be considered as if employed and on duty and will be considered based on their last active assignment, position classification, EEOC classification, length of service, and certification. Employees identified as surplus while on leave will be provided four alternatives: (1) resignation, (2) remain on original leave, (3) change to a RIF leave not to exceed one year, or (4) immediate reemployment with assignment based on displacement. Notices and response delivery rules apply; failure to select by deadline results in termination and loss of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures leave status does not prevent participation in displacement choices; provides options including immediate reemployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III: Displacement and options for personnel with >=3 complete academic years
rubrics_metrics.description: Same procedures as Phase II except contractual personnel being displaced have three or more complete academic years of service; after displacement, employees identified for RIF will have alternatives: (1) resignation, (2) leave of absence, or (3) reclassification to one-half time at one-half salary with all benefits maintained provided there are adequate positions to make this possible. Under one-half time, two employees must be reduced to one-half time for each abolished position; reclassification to full-time occurs in inverse order; upon recall employees have options (resign, eligible leave, or return to full-time). Remaining on one-half time after recall is not an available option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers additional protection (half-time reclassification) for more-senior contractual employees, with explicit mechanics for implementation and recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notification and polling order
rubrics_metrics.description: Once surplus personnel identified by position classification, EEOC classification, RIF level, and certification, surplus personnel will be notified and polled in the order of the longest length of service. The employee with the longest length of service in the surplus personnel category at the highest RIF level will be notified and given four options: (1) resignation, (2) leave of absence not to exceed one year, (3) displacement at an equivalent level if eligible, or (4) displacement at a lower level if eligible. Notices must be delivered by a designee or by registered mail; responses must be in person or registered mail. Failure to select an alternative by the deadline results in termination and loss of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies polling and notification order and reiterates delivery/response requirements and consequences of nonresponse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation notice timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment separation notices due to RIF must be delivered by a designee or by registered mail to the last known address with a postmark not less than thirty calendar days prior to the date of separation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a minimum 30-calendar-day advance notice requirement (postmark standard) for separations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance continuation while on RIF leave
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee on leave of absence due to RIF may continue insurance coverages by prepayment of premiums directly to the insurance companies involved if permitted by the carriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows continuation of benefits at employee expense if carriers permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify Department of Personnel upon obtaining other full-time professional employment
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractual employee who obtains full-time employment in a professional position in a school, college, or university while on a RIF leave must notify the Department of Personnel in writing (in person or by registered mail) immediately. Failure to notify is considered a breach of professional conduct. Upon notification, the employee's leave will be canceled, benefits canceled, and separation considered final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects recall integrity by requiring timely disclosure of new full-time employment; allows employees to hold auxiliary/substitute/part-time positions without affecting recall rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall eligibility and notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees granted RIF leaves as well as employees on other leaves are eligible for reemployment by position classification, EEOC classification, length of service, and certification. Department of Personnel shall notify by telephone when a suitable position is identified; if no telephone contact, notification will be via registered mail to last known address. Employee must accept offer in writing (in person or by registered mail) within ten (10) calendar days from the postmark date; must report for duty within fourteen (14) calendar days of offer if requested by the Superintendent. Failure to accept or report results in cancellation of leave and benefits and final separation. If reemployment occurs within 365 days, sick leave balance is reinstated and salary reestablished at appropriate level; no credit for salary placement for period of absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timelines, methods of contact, consequences of nonresponse, and limited restoration of sick leave and salary placement upon recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: No recall period and leave cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee has not been recalled within 365 calendar days following the date of separation due to RIF, the leave of absence will be canceled, all employment benefits will be canceled, and the employment separation will be considered final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps recall eligibility at 365 days (one year) unless specific extension conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of leave only for certified physical disability
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of the leave of absence resulting from RIF will be considered only in the event of physical disability as certified by a physician licensed in the State of Georgia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a narrow exception to the 365-day recall limit for documented physical disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions that cancel benefits and recall rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits and recall rights are canceled by: voluntary resignation; discharge/termination/nonrenewal; refusal or failure to accept correspondence from the Superintendent; failure to immediately report change in address/telephone; failure to properly respond by established deadlines to written directives regarding RIF; refusal to accept an offer of reemployment by the deadline; failure to maintain valid certification in field employed or displaced to; failure to report for duty on specified date upon reemployment; full-time employment in a professional position while on RIF leave; nonavailability of a suitable position and no recall within 365 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates many specific employee actions/conditions that forfeit recall rights and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification field groupings for RIF
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to overlapping certification, certain certification fields will be considered as single classifications at each grade level for RIF purposes (examples include Kindergarten; Primary I/II/III and Grade 6; combined Grade 7/8 endorsements; grouped subject areas such as biology/science, business education variants, chemistry/science, earth science/science, economics/social science, geography/social science, government/social science, history/social science, physics/science, political science/social science, sociology/behavioral/social science; Art and Physical Education K-7 vs 8-12 groupings; six music classifications by K-7 and 8-12 and type; mental retardation subcategories; speech and language pathology subcategories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which endorsements/fields are treated as equivalent for displacement and service list placement, affecting who can displace whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals rights for RIF decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A teacher with less than three complete academic years of service has no right of appeal. An auxiliary employee has no right of appeal. A teacher with three or more complete academic years of service who has signed a contract for the fourth or later years may appeal the RIF decision to the DeKalb County Board of Education in accordance with Georgia Codes. For midyear termination or end of year termination without notice by April 15, a contractual employee has a right to appeal to the Board per Georgia Codes; an auxiliary employee has no right of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who may appeal RIF decisions, differentiating by length of service, contract status, and timing of termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision authority for RIF procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction in force procedures are subject to revision when necessary to insure accomplishment of the educational aims of the school system and/or to insure compliance with State and/or Federal laws relating to employment decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates procedures may be amended to remain consistent with legal and educational requirements.
